prompt: How do I insert a table of figures in Word?
completion:
Below is a **step‑by‑step guide** (with a few tricks) for inserting a *Table of Figures* in Microsoft Word. I’ll cover the most common workflow (Word 2016/2019/Office 365), but the steps work almost the same in older versions (2007/2010/2013). --- ## 1️⃣ Make sure every figure has a caption A *Table of Figures* pulls its entries from Word’s **Caption** field. If you haven’t captioned your figures yet, do it now: | What you do | Where you find it | Tips | |------------|-------------------|------| | **Insert a picture** | `Insert` → `Pictures` | Place the picture on its own line so the caption is easy to read. | | **Add a caption** | `References` → `Insert Caption` | • Choose the **Label** “Figure” (or create a new label).
• Click **Numbering…** if you want “Figure 1.1” style.
• Click **OK**. | | **Edit the caption** | Click on the caption text | You can edit the caption text directly, but the number will stay correct. | > **Why captions matter** > Word only knows about figures that have a *Caption* field. If you simply write “Figure 1: …” in a paragraph, the table won’t pick it up. --- ## 2️⃣ Insert the Table of Figures 1. **Place the cursor** where you want the table (usually right after the cover page or in a dedicated “Figures” section). 2. Go to the **References** tab. 3. Click **Table of Figures** (Word 2007: `Insert` → `Table of Figures`). 4. In the dialog that opens, set the options: | Option | What it does | |--------|--------------| | **Caption label** | Select “Figure” (or the label you used). | | **Formats** | Choose a preset (e.g., “Figure 1. Heading 2”) or click **Custom** to tweak it. | | **Show page numbers** | Tick if you want page numbers next to each entry. | | **Use hyperlinks** | Tick to make each entry clickable in the PDF or Word file. | | **Leader** | Choose the dots, dashes, or spaces that fill the space between the figure title and page number. | | **Modify…** | Change the style (e.g., font, size) of the entire table if you want a custom look. | 5. Click **OK**. Word inserts a field that looks like: ``` { TOC \o "1-3" \h \z \u } ``` That’s your table of figures! --- ## 3️⃣ Update the table when you add, delete, or move figures - **Right‑click** anywhere in the table. - Choose **Update Field** → **Update entire table** (or simply press **F9**). > **Tip:** Word can update the table automatically when you print or convert to PDF if you enable that in **File** → **Options** → **Advanced** → *Show field codes instead of their values when printing*. (Not usually needed for everyday editing.) --- ## 4️⃣ Advanced tweaks ### 4.1 Add a Table of Figures to the Table of Contents If you want a single **Table of Contents** that includes both headings *and* figures: 1. Go to **References** → **Table of Contents** → **Custom Table of Contents**. 2. Click **Options**. 3. In the *Table of Contents options* dialog, tick **Figure** in the **Styles** list (or any other label you want to include). 4. Click **OK** → **OK** again. The TOC will now list headings *and* figure captions. ### 4.2 Create a new caption label If you want a custom label (e.g., “Fig.” instead of “Figure”): 1. In the **Insert Caption** dialog, click **New Label…**. 2. Type “Fig.” (or anything else). 3. Click **OK** → **OK**. Your new label will appear in the list for future captions. ### 4.3 Custom numbering (Figure 1.1, 1.2, …) 1. While inserting the caption, click **Numbering…**. 2. Check **Include chapter number** and select the heading style that corresponds to the chapter (e.g., Heading 1). 3. Choose the format (e.g., “1.1”). 4. Click **OK**. Now each figure will be numbered “ChapterNumber.FigureNumber”. ### 4.4 Styling the table The table uses the **TOC** style by default, but you can modify it: 1. Select any cell in the table. 2. Go to **Home** → **Styles**. 3. Right‑click **TOC** → **Modify…**. 4. Adjust font, alignment, indentation, etc. (You can also create a new style if you want to keep the original TOC style.) --- ## 5️⃣ Quick keyboard shortcuts | Action | Shortcut (Word 2016/2021/365) | |--------|------------------------------| | Insert caption | `Alt` + `Shift` + `C` (or `Alt` + `N` then `H`) | | Insert Table of Figures | `Alt` + `N` then `O` then `F` | | Update field | `F9` (when the cursor is in the field) | | Toggle field codes | `Alt` + `F9` | | Show/hide field codes | `Ctrl` + `F9` | --- ## 6️⃣ Common pitfalls & solutions | Issue | Likely cause | Fix | |-------|--------------|-----| | Table of figures shows nothing | No captions or captions use a different label | Make sure every figure has a caption with the **Figure** label (or change the label in the Table of Figures dialog). | | Page numbers are wrong | The field wasn’t updated | Right‑click → **Update Field**. | | Caption numbers jump or reset | Numbering format set to restart on each section | Adjust **Numbering…** settings to “Continue from previous section” or “Restart at 1”. | | Table is too wide | Leader style is too short or too long | Change the **Leader** option in the Table of Figures dialog. | --- ## 7️⃣ Quick recap 1. **Caption** every figure (`References` → `Insert Caption`, choose “Figure”). 2. **Insert** the table (`References` → `Table of Figures`). 3. **Update** it after adding/removing figures (`F9` or right‑click → **Update Field**). 4. **Style** it as you like (modify the **TOC** style or create a custom style). 5. (Optional) **Add to** the main Table of Contents or create custom numbering. That’s it! Once you’ve set it up, the Table of Figures will keep itself current automatically whenever you update the field, so you can focus on writing instead of bookkeeping.
